title: Mahatma Gandhi and the Quit India Movement: 'Do or Die' at Gowalia Tank (1942)
summary: On August 8, 1942, at the Gowalia Tank Maidan in Bombay, seventy-two-year-old Mahatma Gandhi issued his historic ultimatum to the British Empire and bestowed the mantra 'Do or Die' upon the Indian nation.
keywords: Historical Dialogue 182: நேருவும் “ஓய்வைப் பற்றி சிந்தித்தேன்” என்ற பதிலும்
full_text:
On the humid evening of August 8, 1942, tens of thousands of citizens packed the Gowalia Tank Maidan in Bombay for the historic session of the All India Congress Committee.

With the Second World War raging and Japanese forces at the eastern borders of India, the British colonial government remained stubbornly entrenched in imperial denial. Seventy-two-year-old Mahatma Gandhi walked to the microphones to deliver what historians consider the most impassioned speech of his life.

Speaking for over two hours into the night, Gandhi's words possessed the thunder of a moral revolution:
"Here is a mantra, a short one, that I give you. You may imprint it on your hearts and let every breath of yours give expression to it: The mantra is: 'Do or Die!'

We shall either free India or die in the attempt; we shall not live to see the perpetuation of our slavery! Let every man and woman consider himself or herself as a free citizen from this moment forward and act as if you are free.
I am not going to be satisfied with anything short of complete freedom. We shall not act hastily, but we shall not retreat! My call to the British rulers is simple, honest, and urgent: In the name of God and humanity, Quit India!"

Before dawn, British police arrested Gandhi and the entire Congress Working Committee. But the spark had been struck. Millions of ordinary citizens rose in an uncontrollable nationwide rebellion that irreversibly signaled the end of the British Empire in Asia.
